text:
Chicago arrives winless in five (0-4-1), outscored 23-11 in that stretch, after a 4-1 loss at Tampa Bay, and is missing Bowen Byram and Patrick Kane. Carolina is 4-1-0 over its last five after beating the Islanders 5-3, though it plays without Jordan Staal. Our model has CAR scoring 3.87 expected goals to CHI's 2.44. The Hurricanes won the first meeting 5-2 on Oct 10, a game they deserved to win 67% of the time.

The chance numbers lean one way. Carolina has taken 58% of the expected goals (the quality of shots) at five on five, Chicago 41%. The Hurricanes also have the better power play, 0.94 expected goals a game to 0.51, and the better penalty kill. In net, Spencer Knight (projected) is at +1.6 goals saved above expected, meaning goals prevented beyond what the shots called for, against +9.5 for Pyotr Kochetkov (projected). Knight was at +11.1 across 55 games last season. Chicago's record is worse than its chances: finishing and goaltending have cost them.

Connor Bedard, Chicago's top power-play option, is at 31% to score and 66% for a point. Roman Kantserov has a seven-game point streak, and Mark Lazerus of The Athletic posted his words on the speed of the NHL: "Everyone is smarter, harder, stronger, faster." For Carolina, Sebastian Aho is 39% to score and 78% for a point, and Jackson Blake has an eight-game point streak and has taken Staal's spot beside Martinook and Ehlers. Our under-the-radar pick is Mark Jankowski, a third-liner with 4.4 expected goals in his last 10 games, at 25% to score and 42% for a point.
